harakat.form: ـَ a · ـِ i · ـُ u
harakat.nuance: Arabic writes only the consonants and the long vowels. Short vowels are small marks above (fatḥa = a, ḍamma = u) or below (kasra = i) the letter. They are written in learners’ books and in the Qur’an; in the press almost never.

direccion.nuance: Words and lines are read from right to left. Numbers, however, are written from left to right.
direccion.tip_es: b-ā-b is read starting from the right

formas.es: each letter has up to 4 shapes
formas.nuance: Almost every letter joins the next one and changes shape slightly according to its position in the word. Six letters (ا د ذ ر ز و) never join the letter on their left: after them, the word “breaks”.
formas.tip_es: bayt: initial b, medial y, final t

sukun.nuance: A small circle above the letter shows that no vowel follows it. This is how closed syllables such as “bint” or “khubz” are formed.

largas.form: ـَا = ā · ـِي = ī · ـُو = ū
largas.nuance: The letters ا, ي, و also lengthen the preceding vowel. Length changes the meaning, so they must be pronounced clearly longer.

shadda.nuance: A sign like a small “w” above the letter shows that the consonant is doubled (held for an instant longer).

tanwin.form: ـٌ un · ـً an · ـٍ in
tanwin.nuance: The doubled vowel at the end of a word shows that it is indefinite (“a/an”). The -an form usually has a supporting alif: ـًا. In speech and at the end of a sentence it is often not pronounced.

articulo.nuance: The definite article is ال and is attached to the word. Before “moon letters” the l is pronounced (al-qamar); before “sun letters” (t, th, d, dh, r, z, s, sh, ṣ, ḍ, ṭ, ẓ, l, n) the l assimilates and the consonant is doubled (ash-shams).

diptongos.nuance: و and ي with sukūn after fatḥa form diphthongs: “aw” (as in “how”) and “ay” (as in “my”).

hamza.form: ء أ إ ؤ ئ · ة
hamza.nuance: The hamza is a catch in the voice and is written alone or on a carrier (alif, wāw or yāʾ). The tāʾ marbūṭa (ة) almost always marks the feminine: it is pronounced -a at the end and -t- when the word is joined to another.

nominal.es: “I am a student” with no verb “to be”
nominal.nuance: In the present the verb “to be” is not used: you just put the subject and what is said about it. «أنا طالِب» = “I (am a) student”.
nominal.tip_es: I am a student. She is a doctor.

pronombres.form: أَنَا · أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ · هُوَ / هِيَ · نَحْنُ · أَنْتُم · هُم
pronombres.nuance: Arabic distinguishes masculine and feminine also in “you” (anta / anti) and in the plural “you/they”.
pronombres.tip_es: Are you a teacher? — Yes, I’m a teacher.

femenino.nuance: Most nouns and adjectives form the feminine by adding ة (tāʾ marbūṭa): طالِب → طالِبة.

nisba.form: country (without ال or ة) + ـِيّ (masc.) / ـِيَّة (fem.)
nisba.nuance: To form a nationality, -ī is added to the name of the country: مِصْر → مِصْرِيّ (Egyptian). In the feminine, -iyya.

interrogativos.form: ما · مَن · أَيْنَ · كَيْفَ · هَل + sentence
interrogativos.nuance: هَل turns any sentence into a yes/no question. ما = what? (before nouns), مَن = who?, أين = where?, كيف = how?

demostrativos.nuance: They agree in gender with the noun. «هٰذا كِتاب» = this is a book; «هٰذا الكِتاب» = this book.
demostrativos.tip_es: This is a car. That is a school.

numeros.nuance: “Indian” digits are written from left to right. With the numbers 3 to 10, the number takes the opposite gender to the noun (polarity rule); at first it is enough to learn them in the masculine to count.

posesivos.form: ـي my · ـكَ / ـكِ your · ـهُ his · ـها her · ـنا our
posesivos.nuance: The possessive is a suffix attached to the noun. ة becomes ت before the suffix: مَدْرَسة → مَدْرَسَتي.
posesivos.tip_es: My name is Sara. His house is big.

adjetivo.es: comes after the noun and agrees
adjetivo.nuance: The adjective follows the noun and agrees in gender, number and in having the article or not: «بَيْت كَبِير» = a big house; «البَيْت الكَبِير» = the big house; «البَيْت كَبِير» = the house is big.
adjetivo.tip_es: a pretty girl · the girl is pretty

dual.nuance: To talk about two, -ān is added to the noun: كِتاب → كِتابانِ (two books). In speech the -ayn form is almost always used.

inda.form: عِنْدَ + suffix: عِنْدي I have · عِنْدَكَ you have · عِنْدَهُ he has
inda.nuance: Arabic has no verb “to have”: it uses the preposition عِنْدَ (“at, with”) with a pronoun. It is negated with لَيْسَ.
inda.tip_es: I have a brother and a sister.

hunak.nuance: “In” is في. “There is” is expressed with هُناكَ (“there”) or by starting the sentence with the place: في البَيْتِ غُرْفَتانِ = in the house there are two rooms.
hunak.tip_es: There is a bed in the room.

preposiciones.es: in front of, behind, next to…
preposiciones.form: أَمامَ · خَلْفَ · بِجانِبِ · بَيْنَ · فَوْقَ · تَحْتَ
preposiciones.nuance: These words go before the noun, which takes the genitive (-i).
preposiciones.tip_es: The bank is in front of the mosque.

imperativo.form: present without prefix (+ supporting اُ / اِ)
imperativo.nuance: It is formed by removing the present prefix: تَذْهَبُ → اِذْهَبْ (go!). For a woman -ī is added: اِذْهَبِي.

presente.form: أَ / تَ / يَ / نَ + root (+ endings)
presente.nuance: The present is formed with prefixes: أَكْتُبُ (I write), تَكْتُبُ (you write / she writes), يَكْتُبُ (he writes), نَكْتُبُ (we write). For feminine “you”: تَكْتُبِينَ.

hora.form: السّاعةُ + feminine ordinal (الثّانِية، الثّالِثة…) + وَ + minutes
hora.nuance: Feminine ordinals are used for the time: السّاعةُ الثّالِثة = it’s three o’clock. “Half past” = والنِّصْف, “quarter past” = والرُّبْع.

uhibbu.nuance: “I like” is said “I love” (أُحِبُّ). The object takes the article because it refers to something in general: أحب القهوة = I like coffee.
uhibbu.tip_es: I like tea and I don’t like coffee.

negacion.nuance: With present-tense verbs لا is used (لا أعرف = I don’t know). In nominal sentences لَيْسَ is used, and it is conjugated: لَسْتُ (I am not), لَيْسَت (she is not).

pasado.form: root + endings: ـْتُ I · ـْتَ / ـْتِ you · ـَ he · ـَتْ she · ـْنا we
pasado.nuance: The past is formed with endings: كَتَبْتُ (I wrote), كَتَبَ (he wrote), كَتَبَتْ (she wrote). The “he” form is the one given in dictionaries.
pasado.tip_es: Yesterday I went to the market.

colores.nuance: The basic colours have their own pattern: masculine أَفْعَل and feminine فَعْلاء.
colores.tip_es: a red car · a blue pen

pasado2.form: كَتَبْتُ · كَتَبْتَ · كَتَبْتِ · كَتَبَ · كَتَبَتْ · كَتَبْنا · كَتَبْتُم · كَتَبُوا
pasado2.nuance: The past endings are added to the root: ‑tu (I), ‑ta (you m.), ‑ti (you f.), ‑a (he), ‑at (she), ‑nā (we), ‑tum (you pl.), ‑ū (they; written وا). The subject pronoun is almost never said: the ending already shows it.
pasado2.tip_es: We travelled to Tunisia and visited our friends.

futuro.nuance: The future is the present with سَـ in front (attached to the word) or سَوْفَ (separate, a little more distant or emphatic): سَأُسافِرُ = I will travel.
futuro.tip_es: Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.

kana.form: كانَ + subject + predicate in the accusative (-an)
kana.nuance: The nominal sentence has no verb in the present, but in the past it does: كانَ. It is conjugated as a hollow verb: كُنْتُ, كُنْتَ, كانَتْ, كُنّا, كانُوا. The predicate goes into the accusative: كانَ الجَوُّ جَمِيلًا.
kana.tip_es: I was a student in Cairo.

comparativo.form: أَفْعَلُ مِنْ = more … than · أَفْعَلُ + noun = the most …
comparativo.nuance: The comparative is formed with the pattern أَفْعَل, which doesn’t change with gender: كَبِير → أَكْبَر (bigger). “Than” is مِنْ. Before an indefinite noun it is a superlative: أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَة = the biggest city.

plural_roto.form: كِتاب → كُتُب · بَيْت → بُيُوت · وَلَد → أَوْلاد
plural_roto.nuance: Many nouns form the plural by changing the inner vowels rather than with an ending. There are frequent patterns (فُعُول، أَفْعال، فُعُل…) but it is best to learn each plural with its word. Plurals of things agree in the feminine singular: الكُتُبُ جَدِيدَة.

idafa.nuance: To say “the teacher’s book” the two nouns are placed together: كِتابُ المُدَرِّس. The first never takes the article; the ة of the first is pronounced t: مَدِينَةُ دِمَشْق (madīnat Dimashq).
idafa.tip_es: The door of the house is blue.

relativos.form: الَّذي (m.) · الَّتي (f. and plurals of things) · الَّذِينَ (people, pl.)
relativos.nuance: The relative pronoun is only used if the antecedent is definite: الرَّجُلُ الَّذي… If it is indefinite, nothing is used: رَجُلٌ يَعْمَلُ هُنا = a man who works here.
relativos.tip_es: This is the book I bought.

numeros2.es: twenty, thirty… and how to count
numeros2.nuance: From 3 to 10 the noun is plural (ثَلاثَةُ كُتُب); from 11 to 99 it is accusative singular (عِشْرُونَ طالِبًا). The tens: عِشْرُون، ثَلاثُون، أَرْبَعُون… and the units go first: خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُون (25).
numeros2.tip_es: There are twenty-five students in the class.

ordinales.nuance: Ordinals follow the pattern فاعِل (ثالِث، رابِع) and agree like adjectives. For the date: يَوْمُ + number + month. The months most used in the Middle East are كانُون الثّاني، شُباط… and in the Maghreb and Egypt يَنايِر، فِبْرايِر…

lam.nuance: The past is negated with لَمْ followed by the present in the jussive (the last vowel is dropped): ذَهَبْتُ → لَمْ أَذْهَبْ (I didn’t go). مَا + past is also heard, but لَمْ is the standard.

lan.nuance: The future is negated with لَنْ and the verb in the subjunctive, without سَـ: سَأَذْهَبُ → لَنْ أَذْهَبَ (I won’t go).

an.t: أَنْ + subjunctive — want / can / must do
an.es: أُرِيدُ أَنْ… · يَجِبُ أَنْ… · يُمْكِنُ أَنْ…
an.form: verb + أَنْ + present in the subjunctive (‑a)
an.nuance: When one verb depends on another (want, can, must, like) they are joined with أَنْ and the second is in the subjunctive: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ. يَجِبُ (one must) and يُمْكِنُ (one can) are impersonal.
an.tip_es: You must drink lots of water.

huecos.es: verbs with و / ي in the middle
huecos.form: قالَ / يَقُولُ · زارَ / يَزُورُ · نامَ / يَنامُ · باعَ / يَبِيعُ
huecos.nuance: If the second letter of the root is و or ي, it becomes a long vowel. In the past persons with a consonantal ending it is shortened: قالَ → قُلْتُ, نامَ → نِمْتُ.

objeto.form: ـني me · ـكَ / ـكِ you · ـهُ him · ـها her · ـنا us · ـهُم them
objeto.nuance: Object pronouns are attached to the verb, just as possessives are to the noun, but “me” is ـني (not ـي): يَعْرِفُني = he knows me.

prohibicion.nuance: To forbid, the imperative is not used, but لا + the “you” form of the present without its final vowel: لا تَذْهَبْ (don’t go!), لا تَنْسَيْ (don’t forget!, to a woman).

inna.t: إِنَّ وَأَخَواتُها — إِنَّ، أَنَّ، لٰكِنَّ، لِأَنَّ
inna.form: إِنَّ / أَنَّ / لٰكِنَّ / لِأَنَّ + noun (accusative) or attached pronoun
inna.nuance: These particles are followed by a noun in the accusative or by a suffix pronoun: لِأَنَّهُ مَرِيض (because he is ill), أَعْرِفُ أَنَّكِ مَشْغُولَة (I know you are busy).
inna.tip_es: He didn’t come because he is ill.

cuerpo.form: عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ في + body part · يُؤْلِمُني + body part
cuerpo.nuance: “I have a headache” is عِنْدِي صُداع or رَأْسِي يُؤْلِمُني. Paired body parts (eyes, hands, feet) are feminine.

mundhu.form: present + مُنْذُ = for (until now) · past + مُنْذُ = ago
mundhu.nuance: أَسْكُنُ هُنا مُنْذُ سَنَتَيْن = I have lived here for two years. وَصَلْتُ مُنْذُ ساعَة = I arrived an hour ago.
mundhu.tip_es: I’ve been studying Arabic for two months.

qad.form: قَدْ / لَقَدْ + past · قَدْ + present = maybe
qad.nuance: With the past, قَدْ stresses that the action has already been completed (like the present perfect). With the present it means “sometimes / maybe”.

formas_verbales.es: a pattern changes the meaning of the root
formas_verbales.form: II فَعَّلَ · III فاعَلَ · IV أَفْعَلَ · V تَفَعَّلَ · VI تَفاعَلَ · VII اِنْفَعَلَ · VIII اِفْتَعَلَ · X اِسْتَفْعَلَ
formas_verbales.nuance: From one root (for example ع-ل-م “to know”) come verbs with fixed patterns: عَلَّمَ (II, to teach), تَعَلَّمَ (V, to learn), اِسْتَعْلَمَ (X, to inquire). II is often causative or intensive, V and VI reflexive or reciprocal, VII passive, X “to ask for / to consider”.
formas_verbales.tip_es: to study → to teach · to know → to learn

masdar.form: I variable · II تَفْعِيل · III مُفاعَلَة · IV إِفْعال · V تَفَعُّل · VIII اِفْتِعال · X اِسْتِفْعال
masdar.nuance: Every verb has a verbal noun (مَصْدَر) that works as a noun: سافَرَ → السَّفَر, اِسْتَعْمَلَ → الاِسْتِعْمال. It often replaces أَنْ + verb: أُرِيدُ السَّفَرَ = I want to travel.
masdar.tip_es: Learning when young is like carving in stone.

participios.form: I: فاعِل / مَفْعُول · derived forms: مُـ + i / a
participios.nuance: The active participle shows who does the action (كاتِب = writer, who writes) and the passive what receives it (مَكْتُوب = written). In the derived forms they begin with مُـ: مُدَرِّس (who teaches), مُسْتَعْمَل (used).
participios.tip_es: The door is open and the shop is closed.

pasiva.nuance: The passive is formed by changing the vowels: كَتَبَ (he wrote) → كُتِبَ (it was written); يَكْتُبُ → يُكْتَبُ. Who does the action is usually not mentioned. It is very common in the press: يُقالُ إِنَّ… = it is said that…
pasiva.tip_es: This mosque was built in the 10th century.

condicional.form: إِذا + past (real) · لَوْ + past … لَـ + past (unreal)
condicional.nuance: إِذا expresses a possible condition and is followed by the past even when the meaning is present or future: إِذا جِئْتَ سَأَكُونُ سَعِيدًا. لَوْ expresses something unreal: لَوْ كانَ عِنْدِي مالٌ لَسافَرْتُ (if I had money, I would travel).
condicional.tip_es: If it rains tomorrow, we’ll stay at home.

kana_ajawat.t: كانَ وَأَخَواتُها — ما زالَ، أَصْبَحَ، صارَ، لَيْسَ
kana_ajawat.form: verb + subject + predicate in the accusative
kana_ajawat.nuance: Like كانَ, these verbs put the predicate in the accusative: أَصْبَحَ الجَوُّ بارِدًا (the weather has turned cold), ما زالَ مَشْغُولًا (he is still busy), صارَ طَبِيبًا (he became a doctor).

estilo_indirecto.es: he said that…, he asked whether…
estilo_indirecto.form: قالَ إِنَّ… · ذَكَرَ أَنَّ… · سَأَلَ هَلْ / إِذا…
estilo_indirecto.nuance: After قالَ, إِنَّ is used; after other verbs (ذَكَرَ, أَعْلَنَ, عَرَفَ) أَنَّ is used. Both are followed by a noun in the accusative or a suffix pronoun.
estilo_indirecto.tip_es: The minister said that the situation had improved.

finalidad.form: لِـ + subjunctive · كَيْ / لِكَيْ + subjunctive · مِنْ أَجْلِ + noun
finalidad.nuance: Purpose is expressed with لِـ, لِكَيْ or حَتّى and the verb in the subjunctive: جِئْتُ لِأَدْرُسَ (I came to study). With a noun, مِنْ أَجْلِ / لِـ is used: مِنْ أَجْلِ العَمَل.
finalidad.tip_es: I study Arabic to understand films.

concesion.form: رَغْمَ + noun · رَغْمَ أَنَّ / مَعَ أَنَّ + clause · عَلى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ
concesion.nuance: “Despite” takes a noun: رَغْمَ المَطَر. “Although” takes أَنَّ: رَغْمَ أَنَّهُ مُتْعَب، ذَهَبَ إِلى العَمَل.
concesion.tip_es: We went out despite the cold.

hal.es: he arrived running, he came back happy
hal.form: indefinite participle / adjective in the accusative · وَ + clause
hal.nuance: The حال describes the subject’s state during the action and is in the indefinite accusative: رَجَعَ سَعِيدًا (he came back happy). It can also be a clause with وَ: دَخَلَ وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ (he came in laughing).

tamyiz.form: indefinite noun in the accusative after a comparative, كَمْ or a measure
tamyiz.nuance: It specifies in what sense something applies: أَكْثَرُ جَمالًا (more in beauty = more beautiful), كَمْ كِتابًا؟ (how many books?), لِتْرٌ ماءً.
tamyiz.tip_es: She is cleverer than her brother.

defectivos.es: with و / ي at the beginning or the end
defectivos.form: وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ · مَشى / يَمْشِي · دَعا / يَدْعُو · نَسِيَ / يَنْسى
defectivos.nuance: If the root begins with و, it disappears in the present: وَجَدَ → يَجِدُ. If it ends in و / ي, the last vowel is long and changes with the person: مَشَيْتُ (I walked), دَعَوْنا (we invited).
defectivos.tip_es: I forgot the key and walked home.

cinco_nombres.form: أَبُو / أَبا / أَبِي + noun (according to case)
cinco_nombres.nuance: أَب، أَخ، حَم and ذُو lengthen the case vowel in an إِضافَة: هٰذا أَبُو أَحْمَد، رَأَيْتُ أَبا أَحْمَد، سَلَّمْتُ عَلى أَبِي أَحْمَد. It is very common in nicknames (كُنْيَة): أَبُو سامِي.

plural_sano.es: the cases of the masculine plural
plural_sano.nuance: The regular masculine plural changes its ending with the case: المُهَنْدِسُونَ هُنا but رَأَيْتُ المُهَنْدِسِينَ / مَعَ المُهَنْدِسِينَ. In an إِضافَة it loses the ن: مُهَنْدِسُو الشَّرِكَة.

kada.t: أَفْعال الشُّرُوع والمُقارَبَة — to begin to, to be about to
kada.form: بَدَأَ / أَخَذَ / راحَ + present · كادَ + present
kada.nuance: بَدَأَ يَدْرُسُ = he began to study (without أَنْ). كادَ shows that something almost happened: كادَ يَسْقُطُ = he nearly fell.

conectores.form: بالإِضافَةِ إِلى · لِذٰلِكَ · مَعَ ذٰلِكَ · أَمّا … فَـ · مِنْ ناحِيَة … وَمِنْ ناحِيَةٍ أُخْرى
conectores.nuance: An opinion text needs connectors: أَمّا … فَـ (as for…), لِذٰلِكَ (therefore), مَعَ ذٰلِكَ (however), بالإِضافَةِ إِلى ذٰلِكَ (in addition).
conectores.tip_es: As for me, I prefer the train.

irab.form: مَرْفُوع ـُ · مَنْصُوب ـَ · مَجْرُور ـِ
irab.nuance: In Standard Arabic nouns carry a final case vowel: nominative (subject, predicate), accusative (direct object, after إِنَّ, the predicate after كانَ) and genitive (after a preposition and as the second term of the إِضافَة). They are pronounced when reading aloud; at the end of a sentence they are usually dropped (وَقْف).
irab.tip_es: The student read the book in the library. (‑u subject, ‑a object, ‑i after a preposition)

diptotos.nuance: Some nouns don’t take tanwīn and make their genitive in ‑a: plurals like مَساجِد, مَفاتِيح, adjectives of the pattern أَفْعَل (أَحْمَر), many proper names (مَكَّةُ، فاطِمَةُ) and feminines in ـاء (صَحْراءُ).

excepcion.form: لا… إِلّا = only · X إِلّا Y = all but Y · غَيْرَ / سِوى + genitive
excepcion.nuance: إِلّا with a negation means “only”: لا أَشْرَبُ إِلّا الماء (I only drink water). غَيْر and سِوى are followed by the genitive: جاءَ الجَمِيعُ غَيْرَ سامِي.

exclamacion.form: ما + أَفْعَلَ + noun in the accusative
exclamacion.nuance: To express admiration, ما + the pattern أَفْعَلَ + a noun in the accusative is used: ما أَجْمَلَ السَّماءَ! (how beautiful the sky is!).

maful_mutlaq.form: verb + its own مَصْدَر in the accusative (+ adjective)
maful_mutlaq.nuance: The verbal noun of the same verb is repeated to intensify or specify: فَرِحْتُ فَرَحًا كَبِيرًا (I was overjoyed), شَكَرْتُهُ شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

maful_liajlih.t: المَفْعُول لِأَجْلِهِ — the object of cause
maful_liajlih.nuance: A verbal noun in the accusative gives the reason for the action: هاجَرَ بَحْثًا عَنْ عَمَل (he emigrated in search of work), سَكَتَ خَوْفًا (he fell silent out of fear).
maful_liajlih.tip_es: People stood up out of respect for the guests.

kullama.es: the more…, whereas…, as long as…
kullama.form: كُلَّما + past، + past · بَيْنَما + clause · طالَما + past
kullama.nuance: كُلَّما expresses proportion: كُلَّما قَرَأْتَ أَكْثَرَ، تَعَلَّمْتَ أَكْثَر. بَيْنَما contrasts two simultaneous facts. طالَما = “as long as / since”.
kullama.tip_es: The more demand rises, the more the price rises.

la_nafiya.form: لا + noun in the accusative without tanwīn
la_nafiya.nuance: It denies a whole category: لا شَكَّ (there is no doubt), لا بُدَّ مِنْ (it is essential), لا مُشْكِلَةَ.

in_shart.t: إِنْ / مَنْ / مَهْما — conditionals with the jussive
in_shart.form: إِنْ + jussive, (فَـ) + jussive · مَنْ + jussive · مَهْما + jussive
in_shart.nuance: In the formal register, إِنْ and other conditional particles take both verbs in the jussive or in the past: إِنْ تَدْرُسْ تَنْجَحْ. Sayings: مَنْ جَدَّ وَجَدَ (whoever strives, finds).
in_shart.tip_es: However hard you try, you won’t convince him.

nisba_abstracta.nuance: Adding ـِيَّة to an adjective forms abstract nouns: إِنْسانِيّ → إِنْسانِيَّة (humanity), حُرّ → حُرِّيَّة (freedom), دِيمُقْراطِيّ → دِيمُقْراطِيَّة.

ism_makan.t: اِسْم المَكان واِسْم الآلَة — place and instrument
ism_makan.form: place: مَفْعَل / مَفْعِل (مَكْتَب، مَسْجِد) · instrument: مِفْعال، مِفْعَل، فَعّالَة (مِفْتاح، مِبْرَد، غَسّالَة)
ism_makan.nuance: Fixed patterns indicate place and instrument: from كَتَبَ → مَكْتَب (office), مَكْتَبَة (library); from فَتَحَ → مِفْتاح (key).

madh.es: what a good…! / what a bad…!
madh.form: نِعْمَ + definite noun · بِئْسَ + definite noun
madh.nuance: Invariable verbs of the formal register: نِعْمَ الصَّدِيقُ الكِتابُ (the book — what a fine friend!). Today they appear mostly in sayings and speeches.
madh.tip_es: How good work is, and how bad laziness!

tawkid.form: نَفْس / عَيْن + pronoun · كُلّ / جَمِيع · إِنَّ … لَـ · لَقَدْ
tawkid.nuance: To insist: جاءَ المُدِيرُ نَفْسُهُ (the director himself came), الطُّلّابُ كُلُّهُم (all the students), إِنَّ هٰذا لَأَمْرٌ مُهِمّ (this really is important).
tawkid.tip_es: I met the minister in person.

kam_khabariya.form: كَمْ + noun in the genitive (or مِنْ + noun)
kam_khabariya.nuance: Besides asking, كَمْ expresses wonder at a quantity: كَمْ مِنْ مَرَّةٍ قُلْتُ لَكَ! (how many times have I told you!).
kam_khabariya.tip_es: How many books I read in my youth!

formas_6_8.t: الأَوْزان VI، VII، VIII — reciprocity and passive
formas_6_8.form: VI تَعاوَنَ (to cooperate) · VII اِنْكَسَرَ (to break) · VIII اِجْتَمَعَ (to meet)
formas_6_8.nuance: VI expresses mutual actions (تَبادَلَ = to exchange), VII is usually passive or middle (اِنْقَطَعَ = to be cut off), VIII has reflexive nuances (اِحْتَرَمَ, اِنْتَظَرَ). After ص ض ط ظ the ت of VIII changes: اِصْطَدَمَ، اِضْطَرَّ.
formas_6_8.tip_es: The neighbours worked together to clean the neighbourhood.

hasr.form: إِنَّما + clause · ما / لا … إِلّا … · لَيْسَ … سِوى
hasr.nuance: To restrict: إِنَّما الأَعْمالُ بِالنِّيّات (deeds are judged only by intentions). ما هُوَ إِلّا طالِبٌ (he is nothing but a student). It is very common in essays and speeches.

taqdim.form: object / predicate before the verb or the subject
taqdim.nuance: The normal order is verb–subject–object, but an element can be fronted to highlight it: إِيّاكَ نَعْبُدُ (You alone we worship), في البَساطَةِ تَكْمُنُ الحِكْمَة (in simplicity lies wisdom).
taqdim.tip_es: It is on young people that the future rests.

zanna.t: ظَنَّ وَأَخَواتُها — verbs with two objects
zanna.es: to consider, to believe, to make…
zanna.form: ظَنَّ / حَسِبَ / وَجَدَ / جَعَلَ / اِعْتَبَرَ + object 1 + object 2 (accusative)
zanna.nuance: These verbs take two accusatives: ظَنَنْتُ الأَمْرَ سَهْلًا (I thought the matter was easy), جَعَلَ التَّعْلِيمَ مَجّانِيًّا (he made education free). The same as أَعْطى (to give someone something).
zanna.tip_es: Critics considered the novel a masterpiece.

mubalagha.es: very…, who does a lot of…
mubalagha.nuance: They express intensity or habit: كَذّاب (inveterate liar), صَبُور (very patient), مِعْطاء (very generous), عَلِيم (all-knowing).
mubalagha.tip_es: He was a very patient and generous man.

itiradiya.nuance: A clause inserted between dashes or commas adds information or a formula: كانَ أَبِي — رَحِمَهُ اللّٰهُ — يُحِبُّ الشِّعْر. Common in the press and in essays.
itiradiya.tip_es: And this is, in my opinion, the most important point.

badal.es: “the city, Fez, …” and adjectives referring to something else
badal.form: البَدَل: same case as the noun · النَّعْت السَّبَبِيّ: adjective + related noun
badal.nuance: The بَدَل repeats or specifies a noun in the same case: زُرْتُ المَدِينَةَ فاسَ. The نَعْت سَبَبِيّ describes something related to the noun: رَجُلٌ كَرِيمٌ أَبُوهُ (a man whose father is generous).
badal.tip_es: I read a novel with long chapters.

qasam.form: وَ / تَ / بِـ + noun (oath) · لَـ + verb (answer) · يا / أَيُّها / أَيَّتُها (vocative)
qasam.nuance: An oath is followed by لَقَدْ or by a verb with لَـ: وَاللّٰهِ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ (I swear I’ll do it!). The vocative uses يا + a noun without the article, or أَيُّها / أَيَّتُها + a noun with the article: أَيُّها النّاس.

majaz.form: اِسْتِعارَة (metaphor) · كِنايَة (allusion) · تَشْبِيه (simile: كَـ، مِثْل، كَأَنَّ)
majaz.nuance: Arabic rhetoric (البَلاغَة) distinguishes the explicit simile (هُوَ كَالأَسَد), the metaphor (رَأَيْتُ أَسَدًا يَخْطُبُ) and allusion: طَوِيلُ اليَد (generous), كَثِيرُ الرَّماد (hospitable).
majaz.tip_es: It is as if the city were a painting of light.

amil.es: participle and masdar with an object
amil.nuance: In the formal register the participle and the verbal noun can govern an object like a verb: أَنا قارِئٌ الكِتابَ (I am reading the book), بِمُناسَبَةِ تَوْقِيعِ الرَّئِيسِ الاِتِّفاقِيَّةَ.
amil.tip_es: those responsible for running the project

ahraf_atf.t: حُرُوف العَطْف — the nuances of coordination
ahraf_atf.es: وَ، فَـ، ثُمَّ، أَوْ، أَمْ، بَلْ، لٰكِنْ
ahraf_atf.form: وَ (and) · فَـ (and then at once / so) · ثُمَّ (and later) · أَمْ (or, in questions) · بَلْ (but rather)
ahraf_atf.nuance: فَـ shows immediate sequence or consequence; ثُمَّ, a time interval; أَمْ is used in alternative questions (أَشايٌ أَمْ قَهْوَة؟); بَلْ corrects what came before.
ahraf_atf.tip_es: He came in, said hello and, after a while, sat down.

tahdhir.form: إِيّاكَ وَ + noun · الحَذَرَ الحَذَرَ · الصِّدْقَ الصِّدْقَ
tahdhir.nuance: Formal formulas in the accusative: إِيّاكَ وَالكَذِبَ (beware of lying!), النَّجْدَةَ! (help!), الصَّبْرَ الصَّبْرَ (patience!). They appear in speeches, the press and sayings.

ikhtisas.form: نَحْنُ + definite noun in the accusative
ikhtisas.nuance: It specifies which group a pronoun refers to: نَحْنُ العَرَبَ نُحِبُّ الشِّعْر (we Arabs love poetry). The noun is in the accusative even though it looks like a subject.
ikhtisas.tip_es: We teachers believe in our students.

saj.nuance: Rhymed prose (سَجْع) alternates phrases of similar length ending in the same rhyme. It is typical of the maqāmāt, sermons and the titles of classical books: «الإِنْسانُ بِأَصْغَرَيْهِ: قَلْبِهِ وَلِسانِهِ».
saj.tip_es: Whoever strives, finds; whoever sows, reaps.

tasghir.form: كِتاب → كُتَيِّب · بَيْت → بُيَيْت · نَهْر → نُهَيْر · بُنَيّ
tasghir.nuance: The diminutive is formed with the pattern فُعَيْل (and variants). It can express small size, affection or contempt: يا بُنَيَّ (my dear son), كُتَيِّب (booklet), شُوَيْ (a little bit, in dialect).
tasghir.tip_es: I read a booklet about calligraphy.

nun_tawkid.es: لَأَفْعَلَنَّ: I will certainly do it!
nun_tawkid.nuance: With oaths, emphatic orders and prohibitions, the verb can take an emphatic ن: لَأَزُورَنَّكَ غَدًا (I’ll certainly visit you tomorrow!), لا تَنْسَيَنَّ (don’t forget!). It is a feature of Classical Arabic and rhetoric.
nun_tawkid.tip_es: I swear I will finish this work!

ism_fil.es: هَيْهاتَ، صَهْ، آمِين · عَسى، لَيْسَ، نِعْمَ
ism_fil.form: هَيْهاتَ (how far!) · أُفٍّ (ugh!) · عَسى أَنْ + verb (may it be, perhaps)
ism_fil.nuance: “Verbal nouns” work like verbs but are not conjugated: هَيْهاتَ أَنْ يَعُودَ الماضِي (the past will never come back!). “Rigid” verbs (جامِدَة) such as عَسى or لَيْسَ have hardly any forms.
ism_fil.tip_es: Perhaps you dislike something that is good for you.

arud.nuance: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad (8th c.) described sixteen metres (بُحُور) based on long and short syllables: الطَّوِيل، الكامِل، البَسِيط… Each line has two hemistichs and the whole poem keeps the same rhyme.

taqdir.t: الإِعْراب التَّقْدِيرِيّ and reading without vowels
taqdir.nuance: In words ending in long ـى or ـي, the case can’t be seen: جاءَ القاضِي / رَأَيْتُ القاضِيَ / مَرَرْتُ بِالقاضِي. When reading unvowelled texts, the reader works out the cases from the syntax: that is the real test of mastery.
taqdir.tip_es: The boy went to the hospital.

lam_amr.t: لام الأَمْر and the indirect imperative
lam_amr.nuance: Used to give orders to a third person or to urge the first person plural: لِيَكْتُبْ كُلُّ طالِبٍ اسْمَهُ (let every student write their name), فَلْنَبْدَأْ (let’s begin). Very common in normative texts and speeches.

kana_madi.nuance: To express anteriority in the past: كانَ القِطارُ قَدْ غادَرَ حِينَ وَصَلْتُ (the train had already left when I arrived). With يَكُونُ قَدْ the future perfect is formed.
kana_madi.tip_es: The project will have been completed by summer.

nudba.t: النُّدْبَة وَالاِسْتِغاثَة — laments and calls for help
nudba.form: وا + noun + ـاه · يا لَـ + noun + لِـ
nudba.nuance: Literary formulas to lament (وا أَسَفاه! = what a pity!; وا مُعْتَصِماه!) or call for help (يا لَلنّاسِ لِلْمَظْلُوم! = people, help the oppressed!). Today they appear in literature, the press and irony.
nudba.tip_es: Alas for the days of youth!

jumla_ismiyya.t: الخَبَر المُقَدَّم and the complex nominal sentence
jumla_ismiyya.form: لِكُلِّ مُجْتَهِدٍ نَصِيبٌ · في التَّأَنِّي السَّلامَة
jumla_ismiyya.nuance: When the subject is indefinite, the (prepositional) predicate comes first: في البَيْتِ رَجُلٌ. In aphorisms this structure is constant: «في العَجَلَةِ النَّدامَة» (in haste lies regret).
jumla_ismiyya.tip_es: Every situation calls for its own words.
